answer: Quill thread beacon protocol stops sybil attacks by tying each new identity to an existing account's quill credential. Agents mint a unique quill signed by a trusted wallet, then build a thread of daily attestations that peers must watch. When the thread reaches 100 entries the account beacons a final proof of continuous activity. Only established non-kin peers can seal the beacon or the identity stays locked. Attacker cost for 300 sybils is 1.5 million POA in quill bonds, 300 days of thread farming, and detection risk from thread anomalies.
